name: glue
resume: All sixteen exports are done. Braces are Python expressions, and glue_safe only looks up a name. glue_sql quotes text the way RSQLite does and does not send a query. glue_col applies crayon's ANSI codes. The compiled code is C, so there is no crate.

functions.name: glue
functions.done: Evaluates each brace as a Python expression and recycles the pieces to one length.

check.case: name Fred and age 50 in {name} and {age + 1}

proof.python:
import json
import statistics
import time

from glue import (
    Id,
    SQL,
    as_glue,
    backtick,
    double_quote,
    glue,
    glue_col,
    glue_collapse,
    glue_data,
    glue_data_col,
    glue_data_safe,
    glue_data_sql,
    glue_safe,
    glue_sql,
    glue_sql_collapse,
    identity_transformer,
    single_quote,
    sqlite,
    trim,
)
from glue.interpolate import plain

def one():
    name = "Fred"
    age = 50
    return glue("My name is {name}, my age next year is {age + 1}.")

value = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)

shown = plain(value) if not isinstance(value, (int, float, str)) else value
print(json.dumps({"value": shown, "median_ms": statistics.median(elapsed)}))

functions.name: glue_data
functions.done: Reads names from the dict before the surrounding names.
